# Dataset
![](images/dataset_ibm.png){style="width: 200px; border-radius:5px;  background-color: white; border: 5px solid white" fig-align="center"}

This section will introduce you to our dataset and how to prepare it for `MaAsLin3` from a `phyloseq` object.

## Rhizosphere soil
![](images/wyoming_flower.png){style="width: 300px; background-color: white;" fig-align="center"}

We will use a new dataset from:

[A comparison of 16S rRNA-gene and 16S rRNA-transcript derived microbial communities in bulk and rhizosphere soils](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1608399/full#h1).

This study aimed to compare the microbial communities of two different types of soil of a Wyoming native plant [*Boechera stricta*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boechera_stricta). These were:

- **Rhizosphere soil:** The soil penetrated by the roots
- **Bulk soil:** The soil not penetrated by the roots

We will use MaAsLin3 to determine the differential abundance and prevalence of bacterial genera between the two soils.

## Jupyter notebook
![](images/jupyter_notebook.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

Create and open a new `jupyter` notebook called "1-Data.ipynb"

::: {.callout-important}
Ensure all notebooks for this part are created in your `~/adv_R_comm/maaslin3` directory.
:::

At the top create a markdown cell with the following headers.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# 1-Data
## Libraries
```

Then load all the libraries we need in a new code cell along with the `phyloseq` object containing our dataset.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Libraries
library("phyloseq")
library("tidyverse")
library("microbiome")
#Data
load("/pub14/tea/nsc206/NEOF/R_community_advanced/rhizo_pseq.RData")
```

Please create other useful markdown cells in this and future notebooks.

## Workflow
![](images/workflow_ibm.png){style="width: 200px; border-radius:5px;  background-color: white; border: 5px solid white" fig-align="center"}

We need 2 `data.frames` for MaAsLin3: 

- genus taxa counts
- metadata

We'll create these in our `jupyter` notebook with four main stages:

1. [Genus aggregation](/maaslin3/genus_aggregation.qmd): Creating a genus count `phyloseq` from our ASV `phyloseq`
2. [Count table](/maaslin3/count_table.qmd): Extracting the genus count table from our genus `phyloseq` and formatting it
3. [Metadata](/maaslin3/metadata.qmd): Extracting the metadata from the `phyloseq` object and setting reference levels in our groupings
4. [Read counts](/maaslin3/read_counts.qmd): Adding read counts/depths to our metadata which are required for prevalence association testing
